title: paged-kv-cache: block allocator reuse & pinning + TTL optimizations
author: Daniel Chen
release_notes: Improved paged KV cache block allocator to reuse freed blocks and respect pinning/TTL semantics; reduces eviction stalls and memory churn. No breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: customer workloads hitting long tail latency due to KV cache eviction stalls and allocator churn under mixed sequence-length traffic. This PR implements allocator reuse, stronger pinning semantics, and TTL-aware eviction to reduce GC-like behavior and stabilize latency.

Changes in this PR (high level): added a block pool that reuses previously freed blocks to avoid repeated allocations; implement per-block pin counts and a fast-path for pinned blocks to avoid eviction races; introduce TTL on block metadata to avoid growing pinned state indefinitely for long-running sessions; tightened allocator lock scope and added per-shard freelists for reduced contention.

Design notes: reuse pool is sharded by block size class and NUMA node; we keep a small bounded LRU for recently freed blocks to avoid reusing blocks with stale GPU memory mappings. Pinning increments a per-block atomic counter and prevents eviction until decremented; TTL background sweeper reduces stale pins from leaked sessions after timeout. Allocator path tries local freelist -> global reuse pool -> new allocation. We also added optimistic try-reserve to avoid blocking hot request paths.

Checklist: [x] allocator reuse pool implementation; [x] pin/unpin APIs and tests; [x] TTL sweeper + metrics; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] benchmark harness updates and perf numbers; [x] canary rollout plan.

Testing & benchmarks: microbenchmarks on c6g-xlarge-equivalent showed 18-26% reduction in 99th percentile generation latency for mixed short/long sequences (batch sizes 1-8). End-to-end throughput improved by ~10% under heavy cache churn. Stress tests with synthetic leak scenarios validated TTL sweeper recovers pinned state within configured window.

Operational notes: new metrics exported: kv_block_reuse_hits, kv_block_reuse_misses, kv_block_pin_count, kv_block_ttl_sweeps, kv_block_evictions. Default TTL is conservative (30m) and configurable via runtime flag.

Rollout plan: deploy to staging -> perf canary on low-traffic region -> 2-week gradual rollout with metric SLOs monitored (99p latency, evictions/sec, reuse ratio). Backout: disable reuse pool flag and restart runtime if unexpected memory regression.

Related: ENG-1428, ENG-1463. This PR is focused on runtime-level improvements and does not change API semantics.
